$comment: The recorded weight of the production bundle, in gzipped bytes, as
`scripts/check-bundle.js` measures it.
THIS IS A RATCHET, NOT A THRESHOLD. The check compares each build against
these numbers and fails when the bundle GROWS -- not when it crosses a
number somebody picked. The two fixed budgets that stood here before
(80.0 kB entry / 260.0 kB total) were picked once with '~12% headroom' and
then answered every later question wrong in both directions: the total sat
18.5 kB over and read as an emergency, while the entry read as fine with
single-digit percent left. A gate with that little room fires on the next
ordinary commit, and the fix is always the same unearned edit -- raise the
number. A ratchet has no number to pick. Weight that arrives has to be
justified in the commit that adds it, which is what the old comment asked
for and had no way to enforce.
IT IS ALSO SELF-PRUNING, on the same reasoning as
`scripts/ci/known_test_failures.json`: a baseline that only ever goes up
rots into a blanket excuse. A build that comes in meaningfully BELOW a
recorded value fails too, and prints the number to write, so a real
reduction is banked instead of quietly becoming somebody's future headroom.
TO CHANGE THESE NUMBERS: run `npm run build` and paste what it prints, in a
commit whose message says what earned the weight. The edit is deliberately
a diff a reviewer can see, which a raised constant inside a script is not.
-- Measure with the gate, not with the build log --------------------------
These are the check's own `zlib.gzipSync` measurements. They are NOT the
numbers in vite's build-output column: vite reports the entry chunk at
79.1 kB where the gate measures 78261 bytes (76.4 kB), a 3.5% disagreement
that no gzip level reproduces (levels 1/6/9 and the default give 86.7 /
76.4 / 76.3 kB). The '1.1 kB of headroom' the entry was believed to have
was read off vite's column; against the gate's own 80 kB the margin was
3.6 kB. Two instruments, two numbers, and the one that decides the build is
this one. Recording measured values rather than reasoning about a picked
threshold is partly why this is a ratchet.
-- What is recorded, and why the total is what it is ----------------------
entry 78261 B (76.4 kB) -- the chunk every visitor pays for before paint.
total 285173 B (278.5 kB) -- every JavaScript chunk, including the route
chunks most visitors never load. The largest single one is the graph
analyzer at 95.3 kB (@xyflow/react, @xyflow/system, dagre), lazily loaded
on one route: a third of the total that a visitor who never opens the
analyzer never downloads. That gap between the two lines is the whole
reason the entry passed while the total did not; it was never duplication.
A module-to-chunk report over the whole build found 386 module ids across
29 chunks with ZERO in more than one chunk, and 23 distinct packages with
ZERO resolved at more than one node_modules path. Rolldown already hoists
what is shared -- the twelve small chunks in the build output ARE that
hoisting. `manualChunks` had nothing to remove, so the weight is real
feature weight: the case panel, the template-review / support /
clarification section families, and the review editor.
